title: Perimeter and gateways — concept map
intro: The network perimeter controls who reaches your workloads. Security groups are stateful Elastic Network Interface (ENI) firewalls. Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) are stateless subnet boundaries with deny rules. Application Load Balancer (ALB), Network Load Balancer (NLB), and Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) route traffic at different OSI layers. API Gateway fronts serverless APIs. AWS WAF and Shield harden the HTTP edge. The full request path ties every hop from client to target.

overviewDiagram.title: Perimeter stack
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TB
  Client[Internet client] --> CF[CloudFront optional]
  CF --> WAF[AWS WAF]
  WAF --> Edge[ALB or API Gateway]
  Edge --> SG1[Edge security group]
  SG1 --> TG[Target group]
  TG --> SG2[Target security group]
  SG2 --> App[EC2 / ECS / Lambda]
  NACL[NACL subnet boundary] -.-> Edge
  NACL -.-> App

conceptCards.title: Security groups
conceptCards.summary: Stateful ENI firewall. Allow-only. SG-to-SG for ALB→target tiers.
conceptCards.example: App SG allows tcp/8080 from ALB SG only

conceptCards.title: Network ACLs
conceptCards.summary: Stateless subnet filter. Numbered allow/deny. Ephemeral return rules needed.
conceptCards.example: Deny known bad CIDR at rule 50

conceptCards.title: ALB / NLB / GWLB
conceptCards.summary: L7 HTTP vs L4 TCP/static IP vs L3 inline inspection.
conceptCards.example: PrivateLink provider NLB; web API on ALB

conceptCards.title: API Gateway
conceptCards.summary: HTTP API for most Lambda REST. REST API for usage plans. WebSocket for live.

conceptCards.title: WAF & Shield
conceptCards.summary: WAF = L7 rules. Shield Standard free DDoS. Advanced = DRT + cost protection.
conceptCards.example: Managed OWASP rule set on CloudFront

conceptCards.title: Full request path
conceptCards.summary: Route53 → CloudFront → WAF → ALB → SG chain → target. Debug per hop.
conceptCards.example: 502 with healthy app → target SG blocks ALB
